title: Jeremiah 48: The Prophecy Against Moab
body:
Read the chapter → [Jeremiah 48](/bible/jeremiah/48)

This session covers [Jeremiah 48](/bible/jeremiah/48) through 51, four chapters that move straight into the salvation of Israel by way of the prophesied destruction of our enemies. Jeremiah lived during the time of Babylon, and here he prophesies against Moab (the so-called Chinese), Ammon (the so-called Japanese), Edom (the so-called white man), Damascus, Kedar and Hazor, Elam (the ancient and modern Persians, the East Indians), and finally Babylon the Chaldeans (modern-day America). This is our redemption. Scripture says a Christian is to accept both the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies, so this reading should be music to your ears.

**[Jeremiah 48:1-2](/bible/jeremiah/48#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/jeremiah/48#v1)</sup> Against Moab thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Woe unto Nebo! for it is spoiled: Kiriathaim is confounded and taken: Misgab is confounded and dismayed.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/jeremiah/48#v2)</sup> There shall be no more praise of Moab: in Heshbon they have devised evil against it; come, and let us cut it off from being a nation. Also thou shalt be cut down, O Madmen; the sword shall pursue thee.

- This is the word of the Most High against Moab. Woe unto Nebo, for it is spoiled; Kiriathaim is confounded and taken. There shall be no more praise of Moab.
- In Heshbon they have devised evil against it: come, let us cut it off from being a nation. These are the Moabites, and God calls the so-called Chinese by that name.

**[Jeremiah 48:3-6](/bible/jeremiah/48#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/jeremiah/48#v3)</sup> A voice of crying shall be from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/jeremiah/48#v4)</sup> Moab is destroyed; her little ones have caused a cry to be heard.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/jeremiah/48#v5)</sup> For in the going up of Luhith continual weeping shall go up; for in the going down of Horonaim the enemies have heard a cry of destruction.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/jeremiah/48#v6)</sup> Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness.

- A voice of crying goes up from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction. Moab is destroyed, and her little ones cause a cry to be heard.
- Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness. There is no standing against the judgment that is coming.

**[Jeremiah 48:7-9](/bible/jeremiah/48#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/jeremiah/48#v7)</sup> For because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken: and Chemosh shall go forth into captivity with his priests and his princes together.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/jeremiah/48#v8)</sup> And the spoiler shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape: the valley also shall perish, and the plain shall be destroyed, as the Lord hath spoken.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/jeremiah/48#v9)</sup> Give wings unto Moab, that it may flee and get away: for the cities thereof shall be desolate, without any to dwell therein.

- Because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken. Chemosh their god goes into captivity with his priests and princes together.
- The spoiler comes upon every city, and no city escapes. The valley perishes and the plain is destroyed, as the Most High has spoken.

**[Jeremiah 48:10](/bible/jeremiah/48#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/jeremiah/48#v10)</sup> Cursed be he that doeth the work of the Lord deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood.

- Cursed be he that doeth the work of the Lord deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood. The work of the Most High is not to be done half-heartedly.

**[Jeremiah 48:11-13](/bible/jeremiah/48#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/jeremiah/48#v11)</sup> Moab hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither hath he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/jeremiah/48#v12)</sup> Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will send unto him wanderers, that shall cause him to wander, and shall empty his vessels, and break their bottles.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/jeremiah/48#v13)</sup> And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth–el their confidence.

- Moab has been at ease from his youth and settled on his lees, never emptied from vessel to vessel, never gone into captivity. Therefore his taste remained in him and his scent is not changed.
- The Most High will send wanderers to empty his vessels and break their bottles, and Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel.

**[Jeremiah 48:14-17](/bible/jeremiah/48#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/jeremiah/48#v14)</sup> How say ye, We are mighty and strong men for the war?
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/jeremiah/48#v15)</sup> Moab is spoiled, and gone up out of her cities, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, saith the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/jeremiah/48#v16)</sup> The calamity of Moab is near to come, and his affliction hasteth fast.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/jeremiah/48#v17)</sup> All ye that are about him, bemoan him; and all ye that know his name, say, How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod!

- How say ye, we are mighty and strong men for the war? Moab is spoiled, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, saith the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts.
- The calamity of Moab is near to come and his affliction hastens fast. All that know his name are to bemoan how the strong staff is broken.

**[Jeremiah 48:18-20](/bible/jeremiah/48#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/jeremiah/48#v18)</sup> Thou daughter that dost inhabit Dibon, come down from thy glory, and sit in thirst; for the spoiler of Moab shall come upon thee, and he shall destroy thy strong holds.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/jeremiah/48#v19)</sup> O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and espy; ask him that fleeth, and her that escapeth, and say, What is done?
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/jeremiah/48#v20)</sup> Moab is confounded; for it is broken down: howl and cry; tell ye it in Arnon, that Moab is spoiled,

- The daughter that inhabits Dibon is told to come down from her glory and sit in thirst, for the spoiler of Moab comes upon her. The inhabitant of Aroer is to stand by the way and ask the one who flees, what is done.
- Moab is confounded, for it is broken down. Howl and cry, and tell it in Arnon that Moab is spoiled.

**[Jeremiah 48:21-25](/bible/jeremiah/48#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/jeremiah/48#v21)</sup> And judgment is come upon the plain country; upon Holon, and upon Jahazah, and upon Mephaath,
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/jeremiah/48#v22)</sup> And upon Dibon, and upon Nebo, and upon Beth–diblathaim,
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/jeremiah/48#v23)</sup> And upon Kiriathaim, and upon Beth–gamul, and upon Beth–meon,
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/jeremiah/48#v24)</sup> And upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/jeremiah/48#v25)</sup> The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, saith the Lord.

- Judgment comes on the whole plain country, city by city, from Holon and Jahazah to Dibon, Nebo, Kiriathaim, Kerioth, and Bozrah, upon all the cities of Moab, far or near.
- The horn of Moab is cut off and her arm is broken. The strength of the nation is taken away by the Most High.

**[Jeremiah 48:26-27](/bible/jeremiah/48#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/jeremiah/48#v26)</sup> Make ye him drunken: for he magnified himself against the Lord: Moab also shall wallow in his vomit, and he also shall be in derision.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/jeremiah/48#v27)</sup> For was not Israel a derision unto thee? was he found among thieves? for since thou spakest of him, thou skippedst for joy.

- Make Moab drunken, for he magnified himself against the Lord, and he shall wallow in his own vomit and be in derision.
- The Most High asks, was not Israel a derision unto thee? Did the Lord not punish his own children? Then what makes the heathen think their time is not going to come? He punishes his own, so he will surely punish the wicked.

**[Jeremiah 48:28-30](/bible/jeremiah/48#v28)**

> <sup>[28](/bible/jeremiah/48#v28)</sup> O ye that dwell in Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that maketh her nest in the sides of the hole’s mouth.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/jeremiah/48#v29)</sup> We have heard the pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/jeremiah/48#v30)</sup> I know his wrath, saith the Lord; but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it.

- The pride of Moab is called out: exceedingly proud, his loftiness, his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart. For all that pride, these Moabites will go back to their proper place and serve the nation of Israel for what they have done.
- The wickedness of Moab against the children of God is real history the American Board of Education does not teach: enslaving us during the Tang Dynasty, feeding the ghettos, and building whole industries off our people. All of it will be manifested and answered for.
  - **[Psalms 60:8](/bible/psalms/60#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/psalms/60#v8)</sup> Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe: Philistia, triumph thou because of me.

    Moab is my washpot; the Most High set them beneath Israel as a servant.
  - **[Isaiah 14:2](/bible/isaiah/14#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/isaiah/14#v2)</sup> And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.

    The house of Israel shall possess the nations for servants and handmaids in the land of the Lord.

**[Jeremiah 48:31-35](/bible/jeremiah/48#v31)**

> <sup>[31](/bible/jeremiah/48#v31)</sup> Therefore will I howl for Moab, and I will cry out for all Moab; mine heart shall mourn for the men of Kir–heres.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/jeremiah/48#v32)</sup> O vine of Sibmah, I will weep for thee with the weeping of Jazer: thy plants are gone over the sea, they reach even to the sea of Jazer: the spoiler is fallen upon thy summer fruits and upon thy vintage.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/jeremiah/48#v33)</sup> And joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field, and from the land of Moab; and I have caused wine to fail from the winepresses: none shall tread with shouting; their shouting shall be no shouting.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/jeremiah/48#v34)</sup> From the cry of Heshbon even unto Elealeh, and even unto Jahaz, have they uttered their voice, from Zoar even unto Horonaim, as an heifer of three years old: for the waters also of Nimrim shall be desolate.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/jeremiah/48#v35)</sup> Moreover I will cause to cease in Moab, saith the Lord, him that offereth in the high places, and him that burneth incense to his gods.

- The Most High declares he will howl and mourn for Moab, for the men of Kir-heres and the vine of Sibmah, because the spoiler is fallen upon the summer fruits and the vintage. Joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field.
- He will cause to cease in Moab him that offereth in the high places and him that burneth incense to his gods. The idolatry is cut off with the people.

**[Jeremiah 48:36-38](/bible/jeremiah/48#v36)**

> <sup>[36](/bible/jeremiah/48#v36)</sup> Therefore mine heart shall sound for Moab like pipes, and mine heart shall sound like pipes for the men of Kir–heres: because the riches that he hath gotten are perished.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/jeremiah/48#v37)</sup> For every head shall be bald, and every beard clipped: upon all the hands shall be cuttings, and upon the loins sackcloth.
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/jeremiah/48#v38)</sup> There shall be lamentation generally upon all the housetops of Moab, and in the streets thereof: for I have broken Moab like a vessel wherein is no pleasure, saith the Lord.

- The heart of the Most High sounds like pipes for Moab, because the riches he has gotten are perished. Every head shall be bald and every beard clipped, with cutting upon the hands and sackcloth upon the loins.
- A good majority of Moab bald their heads and shave their faces rather than keep their beards, the same as the Mongolians right next door to them. There shall be lamenting generally upon the housetops of Moab.

**[Jeremiah 48:39-42](/bible/jeremiah/48#v39)**

> <sup>[39](/bible/jeremiah/48#v39)</sup> They shall howl, saying, How is it broken down! how hath Moab turned the back with shame! so shall Moab be a derision and a dismaying to all them about him.
>
> <sup>[40](/bible/jeremiah/48#v40)</sup> For thus saith the Lord; Behold, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Moab.
>
> <sup>[41](/bible/jeremiah/48#v41)</sup> Kerioth is taken, and the strong holds are surprised, and the mighty men’s hearts in Moab at that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/jeremiah/48#v42)</sup> And Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord.

- Moab is broken like a vessel wherein is no pleasure. They howl, asking how it is broken down, and Moab becomes a derision and a dismay to all around him.
- He that judges shall fly as an eagle and spread his wings over Moab. The mighty men's hearts that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pains, and Moab shall be destroyed from being a people because he magnified himself against the Lord.

**[Jeremiah 48:43-46](/bible/jeremiah/48#v43)**

> <sup>[43](/bible/jeremiah/48#v43)</sup> Fear, and the pit, and the snare, shall be upon thee, O inhabitant of Moab, saith the Lord.
>
> <sup>[44](/bible/jeremiah/48#v44)</sup> He that fleeth from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that getteth up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring upon it, even upon Moab, the year of their visitation, saith the Lord.
>
> <sup>[45](/bible/jeremiah/48#v45)</sup> They that fled stood under the shadow of Heshbon because of the force: but a fire shall come forth out of Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and shall devour the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones.
>
> <sup>[46](/bible/jeremiah/48#v46)</sup> Woe be unto thee, O Moab! the people of Chemosh perisheth: for thy sons are taken captives, and thy daughters captives.

- Fear, the pit, and the snare are upon the inhabitants of Moab. He that flees the fear falls into the pit, and he that climbs out of the pit is taken in the snare; there is no escape from the years of their visitation.
- A fire comes forth out of Heshbon and devours the corner of Moab. Woe unto Moab, for thy sons and thy daughters are taken captives.

**[Jeremiah 48:47](/bible/jeremiah/48#v47)**

> <sup>[47](/bible/jeremiah/48#v47)</sup> Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the Lord. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.

- Yet the Most High will bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days. This has not happened yet, but it will come to pass, for he has spoken it and his word shall not return. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
